summary: SEO-1.1.1 hotfix regression check on web preview: verified all 6 public routes load with zero page/JS errors after the scheduleDedupeHead import+call in src/index.js. Every route emits exactly one <title>, one <meta name=description>, one canonical, one og:title/og:description/og:url and one twitter:title/twitter:description — no duplicate head tags at runtime. Confirmed the preview uses createRoot into an empty #root (no data-prerendered markers present) so scheduleDedupeHead is NOT invoked in this environment, matching the agent-to-agent context. Client-side navigation / → /pricing correctly updates the live title (Wayly · AI... → Pricing · Wayly) with head counts still at 1 for title and description, proving dedupeHead did not strip React-managed live tags.
critical_code_review_comments: Preview environment cannot exercise the actual dedupeHead code path (no react-snap prerender in dev). The fix should be re-validated in a full react-snap-produced build; head-tag doubling can only be reproduced there. This is a known constraint stated by main agent.

/resources/articles/switching-providers logs two generic 'Failed to load resource: 404' console errors (likely missing static assets/images) — unrelated to the SEO change, but worth confirming those assets are shipped.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression only; the real dedupeHead behavior (removing prerendered duplicates) requires a react-snap build, not the dev preview. Preview shows: has_prerendered_marker=0 on every route, root_has_children=true (React CSR mount), title/desc/canonical/og/twitter all count=1, JSON-LD counts 2–7 per page (no exact duplicates evident from head sweep, but only inspected counts, not content-equality). Client-side nav updates title correctly. All 6 requested routes rendered.
